findings.rule: Title block heat treatment field must not be blank when a heat treatment note is specified on the drawing.
findings.reasoning: The title block heat_treatment field is '---' while note N1 explicitly requires case hardening to 55–60 HRC with a 0.8–2 mm case depth. A manufacturer reading only the title block would skip heat treatment entirely, producing a soft part that fails in service.
findings.correction: Update the title block heat_treatment field to reference N1 or state 'Case Harden per Note N1'.

findings.rule: External threads running into a shoulder require an undercut or relief groove so the thread can be cut to full form and a mating nut/face can seat flush.
findings.reasoning: Feature F7 describes an external M20 thread running up to the shoulder with no undercut or relief groove. Without a thread-relief groove the thread cannot be fully formed to the shoulder face, preventing proper assembly of any mating component.
findings.correction: Add a thread-undercut (relief groove) dimension at the shoulder where the M20 thread terminates.

findings.rule: Functional diameters on a sleeve (bearing seats, fits) must carry a tolerance or fit class.
findings.reasoning: The outer diameters ⌀30 (D1, D13) and inner bore diameters ⌀20 (D4, D12) have no explicit tolerances. As functional surfaces of a pin sleeve they will fall back to the general machining tolerance of ±0.5 mm (per the 6–30 mm range), which is far too loose for any press-fit, slip-fit, or bearing-seat application.
findings.correction: Assign appropriate fit-class tolerances (e.g., h6, H7) to all functional outer and inner diameters.

findings.rule: All notes on a released engineering drawing must convey meaningful manufacturing or inspection information.
findings.reasoning: Note N5 contains the text 'YFYFGHYFGHGF', which is gibberish. It indicates an incomplete draft and could confuse the shop floor or quality inspectors.
findings.correction: Delete note N5 or replace it with the intended specification.
